findings.description: Critical: telemetry_process_health declares checks and an index over lifecycle_kind and expires_at, but neither column exists in the table definition, so the contract DDL cannot execute and the promised 24-hour/7-day retention classes cannot be persisted.
findings.resolution: Add constrained lifecycle_kind and expires_at columns before the constraints and index, and enforce the class-specific expiry rule (24 hours for long_running, 7 days for short_lived) rather than only the current generic <=7-day upper bound. Add migration parse/upgrade/downgrade and both lifecycle boundary tests.

findings.description: Critical: ck_pgqueuer_jobs_context_identity still permits missing duplicated correlation fields because PostgreSQL CHECK accepts UNKNOWN: root_job_id/submission_traceparent/trace_id/submission_span_id use nullable '=' comparisons, so a non-null submission_context plus null indexed columns passes instead of proving equality.
findings.resolution: For rows with submission_context, require every non-null canonical duplicate to be present and compare with IS NOT DISTINCT FROM (including the root identifier after explicitly defining root self-reference semantics). Add negative tests for each null duplicate and each mismatched value, while continuing to allow legacy rows only when submission_context itself is null.

findings.description: Critical: the checked-in generated Python model still diverges from OpenAPI's signed-BIGINT bounds: OperationAttemptPage.root_operation_id and next_after_claim_generation and both ownership epoch fields accept 9999999999999999999. The cursor is also modeled as a general non-negative int64 in OpenAPI even though it represents a claim generation capped at 9223372036854775806.
findings.resolution: Regenerate every Python field from the shared OperationId, ClaimGenerationString, and Int64NonNegativeString definitions; use ClaimGenerationString for request/response attempt cursors; and make the drift gate instantiate max, max+1, and cursor/epoch boundary cases across JSON Schema, OpenAPI-derived validation, Python, and TypeScript consumers.

findings.description: Critical: untrusted traceparent is constrained only by length in JSON Schema, OpenAPI, and the generated Pydantic model, and no contract validator requires its embedded trace/span identifiers to match trace_id/span_id. A 55-character non-W3C string or a syntactically valid carrier for a different trace is therefore admitted, enabling trace-correlation spoofing and split audit evidence.
findings.resolution: Specify and generate W3C Trace Context syntax plus non-zero identifier validation, add a model-level semantic validator that the carrier trace ID and parent ID match the explicit canonical fields under the chosen span semantics, validate tracestate syntax, and add malformed/mismatched ingress tests in every generated/runtime contract surface.

findings.description: Nit: the SQL attempt table documents claim-generation headroom but ck_operation_attempt_claim_generation checks only >=0; generation 9223372036854775807 is rejected indirectly by overflow while evaluating claim_generation + 1 rather than by the declared bound.
findings.resolution: Add claim_generation <= 9223372036854775806 to the named constraint so the database contract states the accepted range directly and boundary failures are deterministic.

findings.description: The revision now has a valid acyclic package DAG, repaired coverage and integration write scopes, a concrete resumable six-hour soak, an enforceable process-local telemetry budget, explicit bootstrap inventory, and a materially specified fail-closed Squid egress topology.
findings.resolution: Retain these corrections while fixing the remaining executable SQL and cross-contract validation blockers.
